html:
The Kakatiyas ruled the Telugu-speaking country of the eastern Deccan from 1163 to 1323, from their capital at Warangal. They were the first to bring the uplands of Telangana and the rich coast of Andhra under one government.

Like the Hoysalas they started as vassals of the Western Chalukyas, and declared independence in 1163. Ganapati Deva, who ruled from 1199 to 1262, conquered the coast and gave foreign merchants a written charter of safety at the port of Motupalli.

He had no son and named his daughter Rudrama Devi as heir. She ruled for nearly thirty years, from about 1262, dressed and titled as a king, and put down the nobles who would not accept her. Marco Polo, who touched the coast about 1292, praised her rule.

The dry interior was made to grow rice by building tanks, large reservoirs behind earth dams. Hundreds survive, and some still water fields. The Ramappa temple of 1213, on the World Heritage list since 2021, and the stone gateways of Warangal fort are the dynasty's best buildings. Diamonds came from mines in the kingdom.

Armies of the Delhi Sultanate besieged Warangal in 1310 and took a huge tribute. In 1323 the future Muhammad bin Tughluq captured the city and the last king, Prataparudra, who died on the road to Delhi.
sum: The Kakatiyas ruled the Telugu-speaking country of the eastern Deccan from 1163 to 1323, from their capital at Warangal. They were the first to bring the uplands of Telangana and the rich coast of Andhra under one government.
